title: Latency Galaxy dashboard: p50/p95/p99 split by model + route with streaming vs non-streaming fanout
text:
Latency Galaxy dashboard: p50/p95/p99 split by model + route with streaming vs non-streaming fanout

description:
Goal: Build a new dashboard (Latency Galaxy) that surfaces p50/p95/p99 latency across model x route combinations with a clear split between streaming and non-streaming IO modes. This dashboard will be used by SRE, runtime, and product teams to: (1) quickly detect shifts affecting tail latency for specific model-route pairs, (2) validate rollout impact when we change batching/kv-cache or kernel selection policies, and (3) provide an on-call triage starting point linked to traces and log aggregates.

Scope:
- Aggregations: p50/p95/p99 latency and request count by (model, route, io_mode) over selectable windows (5m/1h/24h).
- Visuals: heatmap matrix (models rows x routes columns) with streaming/non-streaming toggles, small multiples for percentile trend sparklines, and an interactive cohort selector to compare request-shape buckets.
- Tracing hooks: each cell links to the relevant trace query with prefilled filters (model, route, io_mode, time window).
- Logs/metrics pipeline: use the new observability-tags (model, route, io_mode, request_shape) emitted from ingress to ensure consistent joins. Work includes metrics rename migration and a short-term compensating query for legacy names.
- Alerts: on p99 increase >20% for any model-route io_mode sustained for 10m, route-level error-rate correlation panel.

Out of scope for this ticket: RBAC for dashboard access, long-term retention changes, and automated corrective rollouts. Those will be follow-ups if we identify a repeatable remediation path.

acceptance_criteria:
Dashboard exists under Observability > Latency Galaxy and is visible to SRE and Runtime squads
Heatmap shows p50/p95/p99 for all production models and routes (data accuracy validated against our raw traces for a sample window)
Streaming vs non-streaming toggle correctly partitions metrics and updates all panels within 2s
Each heatmap cell has a working "Drill-to-trace" link that prefilters traces with model/route/io_mode, and opens at least 5 representative traces for the selected window
New metrics pipeline tags are documented and a transitional query is provided for old metric names
Alert rule defined in PagerDuty-oncall project with an annotated runbook link

tasks:
Add io_mode tag to ingress metrics emitter (code change + migration note)
Create aggregation rollup job for model-route percentiles in metrics store
Design heatmap and small-multiple layouts with design (Anika Bose) and implement in Observability UI
Wire tracing link generator to use trace-service query params
Add dashboard-level controls: time window, percentile selector, streaming toggle
Create one-off data validation job comparing new aggregates against raw traces for last 72h
Define and create PagerDuty alert + runbook
PRs: metrics-change, UI dashboard, trace-link helper, aggregation job

notes:
Trade-offs: precomputing p99s reduces UI latency but increases ingestion costs; opted for nearline rollup at 1m buckets to balance cost/latency.
KV cache/batching teams requested an additional per-model 'prefix hit rate' metric — logged as follow-up ENG-312346.
We will surface request_shape cohorts (small, medium, long) but the initial release will use heuristics instead of a ML-based classifier to avoid pipeline complexity.
If streaming tagging is incomplete for older routes, dashboard will show 'partial data' badge and fallback to trace sampling comparisons.
Metric naming: agreed on metrics.redwood.latency.{percentile} with labels model, route, io_mode. Ops will run a migration alias for 30 days.
